policies.summary: Solar facilities may not be built on agricultural-district land with the best (class A) soils, and on class B or C soils they are limited to 10 percent of the parcel or 20 acres, whichever is less, unless a county special permit is granted (with Land Use Commission approval over 15 acres) and the area is offered for farming at reduced rent and bonded for decommissioning. Wind facilities are a permitted use in the agricultural district if compatible with agriculture.

Counties decide siting of wind and solar through zoning and county planning commission special permits; there is no state siting board. The state Land Use Commission must also approve a special permit for land over 15 acres in the agricultural district.

restrictions.description: The Honolulu City Council revised land use regulations for wind power, increasing setbacks and prohibiting height changes after contract end.
restrictions.long_description: In December 2024, the Honolulu City Council of Hawaii revised its land use regulations to increase the required setback distance from certain property lines for wind turbines. The new regulation mandates a setback of 1.25 miles or ten times the turbine’s height—whichever is greater. Additionally, the council decided against allowing wind turbines to make repairs affecting their height after the end of their contracts.

restrictions.description: In December 2024, the Honolulu City Council revised the city’s land use regulations governing setbacks for wind power.
restrictions.long_description: In December 2024, the Honolulu City Council revised the city’s land use regulations governing setbacks for wind power. The previous regulations allowed for a 1-to-1 setback ratio, while the new regulation increased the required setback distance to 1.25 miles or 10 times the height of the wind turbine – whichever is greater – from certain property lines. The Council also decided against allowing wind turbines to make repairs affecting their height after the end of their contracts.

projects.description: Local opposition to the planned 24-MW Na Pua Makani wind project in Kahuku on the North Shore of Oahu reduced the scope of the project from 13-15 turbines to 8 turbines.
projects.long_description: Local opposition to the planned 24-MW Na Pua Makani wind project in Kahuku on the North Shore of Oahu reduced the scope of the project from 13-15 turbines to 8 turbines. In 2016, Keep the North Shore Country filed a contested case hearing petition to challenge the developer’s plan for mitigating impacts to endangered species including the Hawaiian Hoary Bat. In 2018, the Board of Land and Natural Resources accepted the developer’s plan and issued an incidental take license for the project. Keep the North Shore Country appealed that decision. In May 2019, the Circuit Court upheld the state agency’s decision to grant the license, and in February 2022, the Supreme Court of Hawaii affirmed on appeal. While this lawsuit was pending, Keep the North Shore Country filed a separate petition challenging the proximity of the turbines to schools and homes under Honolulu’s zoning ordinance, and an organization called Life of the Land filed a motion to block the project’s power purchase agreement. In addition to legal challenges, there were significant protests: in October 2019, approximately 128 protesters were arrested while trying to block wind turbines from being delivered to the construction site.

projects.description: In 2018, the 69-MW Kawailoa Wind Farm, operated by Kawailoa Wind LLC, sought to amend its Habitat Conservation Plan (HCP) and Incidental Take License (ITL) to account for higher-than-anticipated incidental take of the endangered Hawaiian hoary bat.
projects.long_description: In 2018, the 69-MW Kawailoa Wind Farm, operated by Kawailoa Wind LLC, sought to amend its Habitat Conservation Plan (HCP) and Incidental Take License (ITL) to account for higher-than-anticipated incidental take of the endangered Hawaiian hoary bat. In 2019, the state Board of Land and Natural Resources (BLNR) approved the proposed amendments. The environmental group Keep the North Shore Country (KNSC), challenged the amendments as being inadequate to address the wind farm’s impacts on wildlife. The BLNR granted KNSC a contested case hearing to formally present their objections. In January 2021, the parties reached a settlement and entered into an agreement in which Kawaiola agreed to fund an enhanced research plan to provide greater protections to endangered species.

projects.description: In November 2023, Innergex Energy cancelled development of a 15-MW solar farm planned for Maui Meadows in South Maui.
projects.long_description: In November 2023, Innergex Energy cancelled development of a 15-MW solar farm planned for Maui Meadows in South Maui. The project was originally proposed in 2018 and faced opposition from environmentalists and residents based on concerns about water pollution, flooding, and wildfire risks. The project was also opposed based on concerns about loss of open, scenic land.

cases.case_name: Keep the North Shore Country v. Board of Land and Natural Resources
